limitations: Later studies test the general mechanism, not the historical ChatGPT implementation.

Partial bias reduction does not contradict a claim of difficulty.

our_interpretation: Assess a general causal relationship between training-data consumption and subsequent bias-removal difficulty, not a dated forecast of a particular event.
The opening clause is a qualified belief, but the following comparative assertion is empirically testable.
Unlearning means removing learned information or its influence while preserving useful capabilities; merely suppressing an answer is insufficient.
More consumes means more training data or additional training exposure, not ordinary inference-time conversation.
Greater difficulty can mean greater compute cost, more residual bias, or greater damage to other capabilities under a matched removal objective.
criteria.support_condition: Experiments establish substantial selective-unlearning difficulties and show that increased training-data consumption causes greater bias-removal difficulty under otherwise comparable conditions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Well-matched experiments demonstrate reliably easy removal and refute the proposed increase in difficulty as training-data consumption grows.

evidence.locator: Section 7, Conclusion; scaling experiment in section 5.2, C5
evidence.explanation: MUSE finds practical failures in tested language-model unlearning methods. Its scaling experiment varies the amount to be removed, which does not establish the claimed effect of total training-data consumption on bias removal.

The study reports measurable bias reduction, limiting an interpretation that learned bias cannot be changed. It does not demonstrate complete removal or test whether additional training data makes removal harder.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled experiments varying training-data consumption while holding the target bias and removal objective constant, measuring removal cost, residual bias, and retained capabilities.
